newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ManFed concerned by strong currency trend.
newsitem.headline: NZ ManFed concerned by strong currency trend.

text.p: New Zealand Manufacturers Federation Chief Executive Simon Arnold on Monday reiterated concerns about the strength of the Kiwi dollar.

"It's not so much the short-term fluctuations in the dollar, it's the longer-term trend, and the trend is for the currency to be strongly overvalued at the present time," Arnold told Radio New Zealand.
"What that does is it hits export earnings, and that will in the long term slow down investment in the economy and our longer-term growth outlook," he said.
The New Zealand dollar opened slightly firmer on Monday at US$0.7094/01 and 68.73 on its Trade-Weighted Index, which is at its highest levels since late 1987.

Arnold said that with 40 percent of New Zealand manufactured exports sold to Australia, he was concerned by both the Kiwi's strength against the Australian dollar and the muted Australian growth outlook.

He said the additional spending planned by New Zealand's new centre-right coalition government would encourage the domestic economy to grow but stimulate inflation, thereby holding up the New Zealand dollar and holding down export returns.
He called for a thorough review of expenditure by the new coalition. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
